blurb: Fires when one of your units explores a Ruins tile. One story is drawn by weight from those whose conditions are met; the percentage is each story's share of the eligible-by-weight pool.

events.name: Chosen Child

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

options.text: Adopt the child as my own.
I have no interest in mysterious children.

events.text: In the ruins of a decaying, rune-carved temple your scouts discover a dying priestess and a young child. With her final words she entreats the scouts to bring you the child, saying he is destined to change the world.

events.name: New Humans

options.text: Destroy all evidence of these creatures.
Send scholars and scientists to investigate.
Leave this ill-fated place.

events.text: On a small jungle-covered island off the coast, our explorers discover a cave deep in the leafy undergrowth. Inside, buried in a series of shallow graves, lie the skeletal remains of several hundred ancient villagers. Only these skeletons are much smaller than humans. Your scientific advisors are astonished. Are these beings evidence of early ancestors, or of something much more sinister?

events.name: Raised Fields

options.text: Plow the fields for whatever is left.
Allow scientists to study the process.

events.text: Our explorers discover the ruins of a sprawling agricultural civilization. Raised fields split by shallow canals suggest that the ancient inhabitants used controlled flooding, allowing them to thrive during seasons of heavy rainfall. Such a site has much to teach us about efficient food production, if we take the time to heed it.

events.name: Strange Medicine

requirements.label: Insane / Foolish
tip: The leader must have one of: Insane; Foolish

options.text: That quicksilver is very shiny.

outcomes.label: Ruins Strange Medicine Option Herbs Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Highlander Herbs
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Highlander Herbs Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Willow Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Ranger Bark Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Blessed Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Herbs Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Highlander Herbs
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Highlander Herbs Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Willow Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Ranger Bark Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Blessed Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Herbs Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Highlander Herbs
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Highlander Herbs Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Willow Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Ranger Bark Severely Ill
Ruins Strange Medicine Option Blessed Severely Ill

options.text: I’m not wagering my life on unproven remedies!

events.text: [rival]'s healers have so far made little progress in treating your illness. Driven by growing concern, those close to you begin searching for foreign remedies. Near the crumbling ruins of an abandoned settlement, our scouts encounter an eccentric woman tending a large, overstuffed basket. Her accent is unfamiliar, her dress strange. The woman claims to be a healer and shows us a variety of exotic herbs and unusual substances. She seems harmless and is eager to help. Our scouts return with several treatment options. Which shall we try?

events.name: The World on a Wall

outcomes.label: Ruins On The Wall Ambition Explore
Ruins On The Wall Ambition Reveal
Ruins On The Wall Ambition Reveal2

options.text: Spend time studying the maps of the area.

events.text: Entering into the broken ruins, the paintings covering a single wall stand untouched by the water and the wind. What first looks like a repeating pattern reveals itself as a map of the local lands, with towns and paths long since gone. It is incredible how much of the world is yet to be seen. How will you use this inspiration from those who came before?

events.name: Called by the Gods

options.text: Study the art of divination and communing with the gods.
Reject the priest's teachings.

events.text: The ruins are home to a god, long forgotten to any but the lone priest who tends to the fading shrine. "You have abandoned your birthright: the gift of perception." The priest croaks when brought before you, "The gods know the divine order of the world and it is theirs to judge. Would you argue with the earth? With the heavens?" [character] is taken with the words of the priest and asks the court to find wise men and women to divine the wills of the gods of your ancestors.

events.name: The Gods of [rival]

options.text: Teach us your ways so we can divine the will of the gods!
Seek to understand the gods on your own terms.

events.text: Your [unit] find a priestess attending a roughly crafted statue of the being your people have started to call <p.is_sub.S2=SUBJECT_PLAYER_ASSYRIA>Assur<p=SUBJECT_PLAYER_BABYLONIA>Marduk<p=SUBJECT_PLAYER_CARTHAGE>Melqart<p=SUBJECT_PLAYER_EGYPT>Amun<p=SUBJECT_PLAYER_GREECE>Zeus<p=SUBJECT_PLAYER_HITTITE>Tarhun<p=SUBJECT_PLAYER_PERSIA>Atar<p=SUBJECT_PLAYER_ROME>Jupiter<else>the highest of gods<end>. "The gods are fickle and need appeasing. I can teach you the rituals to gain their favor and avoid their wrath." Will you learn the secrets of Divination?

events.name: Community

options.text: Invite the [religion] to share their ways.
Use the community as a base to explore the area before moving on.
Instruct them to loot what they can from the community.

events.text: Your [unit] send word of their shock upon finding the ruins inhabited by a [religion] community. Although small, the commune has people from different nations living together under's laws. The charismatic leader offered your people food and a place to stay as they explore the surrounding area. What direction do you send back?

events.name: Where an Oar has No Name

options.text: Invite him to return to [city], it is close enough that the gods will understand.
Ask to learn more of this 'oar' and its uses.
Leave the man, such a task must have been for doing something terrible.

events.text: Sitting by the side of the road is a traveler, only a few straps remaining on his well-worn sandals. But the attention of your [unit] is on the wooden pole resting beside the threadbare man. Thicker than a spear and twice as long, the wood flattens out at one end rather than carrying the usual metal point. "Friends, can you tell me what this is?" he asks. When they say they cannot, the weary traveler lets out a deep sigh of relief and pain. "Then I can finally rest. The gods have decreed that this is where I must settle!"

events.name: Ancient Supplies

options.text: Equip your [unit] with the ancient shields, leather pulled taut across a wooden frame.
Take the saddles, incredibly lightweight and pliable to avoid tiring the horse.
The longbows have an immense pull weight, able to fire across great distances.
Send the equipment for study, to see what may be gleaned from this discovery.

events.text: Exploring the ruins, you find a hidden chamber that appears to be an ancient armory. Shields and spears line the walls, decorated with unfamiliar patterns and creatures. Although old, the equipment is sturdy and incredibly strong. Your [unit] stock up, ready for the road ahead.

events.name: Beads and Figurines

options.text: Scientists will forge the future.
Scholars will illuminate the past.
Give the beads to [character], and the figurines to our children.

events.text: Our explorers find tiny beads and copper figurines among the ruins, proof that the previous inhabitants understood how to extract metals from ore. Scientists insist that we could unlock new methods of metal production while scholars argue that they could dispel the mysteries of a forgotten civilization.

events.name: Early Disciples

options.text: Return the temple to its former glory.
Use the rubble for needed supplies.
Ignore the ruins and move on.

events.text: High on the sea cliffs, a circle of round stone ruins gazes out over the crashing waves. The inhabitants of these lone, isolated dwellings must have desired true serenity. One explorer recognizes familiar symbols in nearby cave carvings: what could be seen as early icons of [religion]. Perhaps the site was a primitive temple or monastery of its followers.

events.name: Fruit Trees

options.text: Take the fruit home.
Chop down the trees.

events.text: Blossoming trees tower over the dusty ruins, providing ample shade; their branches are heavy with ripe fruit. A natural orchard stretches for miles. How will you use this excellent source of food?

events.name: Grave Circle

options.text: Make a gift of treasure to the [family].
Add all valuables to the nation's coffers.

events.text: A grave circle in the trees appears to have belonged to a great tribe. The shaft includes the remains of a ruler, his spouse and children, and a retinue of servants. Foreign ruins - and their treasures - have captured the imagination of the nobility, especially the [family]. You might consider using some of the recent findings to gain their favor. Or not.

events.name: In the Clouds

options.text: Restore the ancient [tribe] site.
Forage for valuable materials.

events.text: A massive edifice surrounds this hilltop “city in the clouds,” which looks to have housed many thousands of citizens. Shattered by tree roots and overgrown with dense foliage, this settlement appears to have been an early [tribe] capital. Restoring the crumbling ruin might improve relations, or it could end up a waste of our precious resources.

events.name: Interference

options.text: We will honor [character] with a place in court.

events.text: Our scouts first spot the raised tower of the ruined fortification from a nearby valley, where traces of ancient hunters scatter the ground. They discover a crumbling defensive settlement dominating the cliffs, its storerooms still packed with goods. Unexpectedly, [character] and members of the [family] family send agents to prevent the acquisition of these treasures. "The [family] are repeatedly given the leftovers from these expensive scouting expeditions. We demand more of the spoils."

events.name: Sunken Tombs

options.text: Mount an undersea expedition.
Search the coastal rubble.

events.text: A series of stone-cut tombs line the seaside cliffs. While most of the ruins appear to have been looted, many have sunken beneath the tidal waters, the result of frequent earthquakes. Your scouts can scour the rubble for valuables, or you may hire small craft to explore the shallows.

events.name: The Floating City

options.text: Claim the boats for research.
Send divers to search for treasure.

events.text: A great floating city once clung to this desert coastline, a collection of harbors linked by ferries, bridges, and pontoons. Sadly, much of its splendor now lies lost along the sea floor. Flooding appears to have liquefied the clay islands on which the city stood, sinking it over centuries. Several ceremonial boats remain on the abandoned shore, but the ruins themselves are almost entirely underwater.

events.name: The Watchers

options.text: We shall avoid these ruins... to be safe.
The stone and ore are too valuable to waste.

events.text: In the center of the ruins, high atop a hill, stands a ring of monolithic human figures. The faces gaze out over the nearby fields as if to watch over those below. According to our explorers, the towering figures warn against incursion into these ancient lands. Local tribes are known to keep their distance.

events.name: Hidden Jewels

options.text: Keep the jewels but continue exploring.
The Treasury would be grateful if we found more jewels.

events.text: Our explorers discover a cache of jewels hidden deep in the abandoned ruins. Their orders were to explore the lands. Would you rather they exploit this discovery instead?

events.name: The Diviner

options.text: Such an offer cannot be ignored.
Order scribes to collect her predictions.
Demand a message from the gods.

events.text: A woman, [character] sits upon a crumbling dais in the center of the ruins, arms raised to the heavens. "I have been waiting for you," she says, as she inhales fumes from a stone dish. She claims to be a seer and oracle, a voice of the divine. "I will serve you faithfully until the end of your reign."

events.name: Treasure Hunting

options.text: I think I can make it!
It is not worth the risk, see what else can be gathered.
Search around, there may be other chambers with treasure.

events.text: You lead the [unit] through the ruins, placing each foot carefully as you traverse the dry and flaking rubble. An excited exclamation from one of your scouts brings your attention to a hidden tunnel, the entrance of which has been obscured by a collapsed pillar. As you strain to peer through the small gap, an unmistakable gleam comes from within. There is a small gap, just large enough to squeeze through, but even as you consider it a cascade of dust and stones fall from the roof. The structure looks likely to collapse at any moment. Is it worth the risk?

events.name: Weary Marauders

options.text: We could use help against the [tribe].
Promise them a job, then use them in the riskiest areas while your own troops stay safe.

events.text: Our troops are approached by weary raiders who have been roaming the forests aimlessly. They wish to fight for a worthy cause with us.

events.name: Burly Smith

options.text: Learn her trade.
Loot her metal stores.

events.text: A burly smith maintains an ancient forge in the ruins. She explains that she trades iron weapons to nomads in exchange for food. As long as you don't touch her stockpile of ore, she is willing to share her expertise with you. What do you say?

events.name: Elderly Couple

options.text: Stay and help them reconstruct.
Their leaders are more valuable to us.

events.text: Our explorers come across a group of people inhabiting the ruins, led by an elderly couple. The couple claim that they were once the chief scribe and head priestess of the great sacked city. They ask for our help. What would you have us do?

events.name: Frightened Families

options.text: Join us, and we will protect you.
Send our fighters to face the raiders.
Give us guides, and we will pay off your tormentors.

events.text: A caravan of frightened families approaches our explorers. They explain that bloodthirsty raiders have been preying on them, and they look to you for protection. How shall we help them?

events.name: Geoglyphs

options.text: Create a national historic monument.
Excavate the site to search for valuables.

events.text: Nothing about the hulking dirt mounds seems impressive at first. Not until our troops explore the adjacent desert hills do they return with news. At a distance, these primitive ruins comprise a massive pattern - designs, and even zoological images - made to be seen from a great height. Who knows what riches lie beneath the mounds, but to dig would destroy their beauty.

events.name: Gold Workers

options.text: Increase the treasury.
Send it to our troops.
Study the craftsmanship.

events.text: This hidden jungle city boasts a hoard of gold jewelry: pendants, lip-plugs, nose ornaments, necklaces, and earrings. All the workmanship at the site displays the same signature style and an unparalleled skill with gold. Such a trove of gold is always welcome. Of course, there are many ways to utilize it.

events.name: Good Fences

options.text: Sounds like a fair trade.
We can offer some in exchange for meat.
Would they consider working for us?

events.text: Small gardens dot the ruins, clearly the work of skilled farmers. Emerging from a nearby cave, these expert growers offer to teach us how to build good pastures. All they ask for in exchange is enough wood to repair their shelters. How will you respond?

events.name: Haunted Quarry

options.text: Examine the quarry to figure out how it was made.
Haul back as much stone as we can.
Leave this ill-fated place.

events.text: We stumble upon what looks like an old quarry. The equipment inside suggests an advanced knowledge of engineering. However, nearby villagers claim that furious spirits devoured the miners, leaving the tunnels abandoned.

events.name: Heaven and Earth

options.text: My mind is open...
I want no part in such rituals.

events.text: A temple stands atop the crest of the highest hill, its terrace decorated with bright metal and ceramic. Local legend marks this site as where heaven and earth meet, "where all life began." Of course, the only way to see its wonders is to inhale some of the mind-altering plants along the hillside in an ancient spiritual ceremony. A soldier brings you a bowl of this strange powder, but he seems hesitant about its effects.

events.name: Tribal Hunters

options.text: Kill them and take their supplies.
Invite them to settle with us.

events.text: As our explorers stand by unnoticed, a tribe of hunters visits the ruins to check their traps. They go about their business, distracted by their abundant spoils. Should our explorers intervene?

events.name: Wise Man

options.text: Heed his advice on war.
Heed his advice on trade.
Trust only your own instincts.

events.text: While exploring the ruins, our scouts are approached by an old, one-eyed man who offers to advise you on certain subjects. The scouts are keen to leave the area due to sighting several unusually large wolves, so there is only a short time to talk.

events.name: Ancient Barbarians

options.text: I do not want to offend the [tribe].
We will make good use of what we find.

events.text: Our men find murals depicting creatures, rituals, and battles. The style is reminiscent of the [tribe], leading us to believe that this tribe was perhaps a precursor to their own. Our troops warn against desecrating such a site. The [tribe] are very protective of their culture. Of course, there is much to be learned from these ruins.

events.name: Ancient Site

options.text: Raze the city. We could use the Stone.
Preserve the site and learn its history.

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

options.text: We are stepping onto a holy site. Make an offering to their gods.

events.text: Our expedition comes upon a site that looks like the ceremonial capital of some ancient world. An altar centers the court, and ten thrones sit on each side.

events.name: Buried Treasure

options.text: Let's spend what we need to in order to get this mine operational again.
Sadly, our treasury cannot bear the expense at the moment.

events.text: Your scouts stumble across an ancient, long abandoned structure that appears to have once been a village surrounding a mine. Upon investigation, your wise men inform you that the substance mined here was kaolinite, and that the vein has not yet been exhausted. It would take an investment to get the mine back to operational but the result would be that your craftsmen could make the most extraordinary pottery. What say you?

events.name: Carved Wall

options.text: Advise? I command! Bring the wall to [city]!
I am glad I have such wise generals, I highly value their service.

events.text: Our troops discover a towering wall depicting images and carvings belonging to an ancient civilization with an impeccable record of their laws. Our generals want to preserve such findings. What do you advise?

events.name: City of Clay

requirements.label: Superstitious / Pious
tip: The leader must have one of: Superstitious; Pious

options.text: We must pray that such a fate never befalls us.
The land can change. Let us use it to prepare whilst we can.
Send people to fully unearth the ruins.

events.text: The [unit] report a sea of sun-baked clay, broken brick buildings ordered neatly into streets and wide thoroughfares. It is clear that the people that once lived here meticulously planned the layout of the city, with areas for storing grain, bathing, worship, and fragments of written across shards of pottery. The impressive shell of a city lies deserted. What could have driven such an advanced civilization out of this place?

events.name: Comet Sighted

options.text: It's an omen!
A fascinating observation!
It is none of our concern.

events.text: Our scouts didn’t discover anything interesting in these ruins, however they report that while they were searching them they witnessed a large comet streak across the sky above.

events.name: Cursed Land

options.text: Fill the pit with rocks!
We should study this pit.

events.text: Our scouts report that this area is cursed and blighted. Little vegetation grows here, and there are no animals to be seen. A foul smell hangs in the air, and ghastly moans can be heard throughout the region. At the center of the cursed land they discover a deep pit in the ground, which seems to be the source of the moans and stench. Peering over the edge, they can see fires burning deep below the earth.

events.name: Despoiled Ruins

options.text: Stone for construction.
Iron for our troops.
Wood is always useful.

events.text: Scavenging through the ruins, we find significant amounts of stone, iron, and wood. However, local raiders could reach the ruins by nightfall. We can't fight them off, but we can carry some of the loot back home. Which of the three would you like us to bring back?

events.name: Emerald Mines

options.text: We must reopen the mines.
Leave the old mines alone.

events.text: Explorers uncover numerous shafts in the desert hillside, their entrances covered by past landslides. Emeralds litter the dark passages, suggesting that this site once was a thriving mine. Your scout wishes to continue excavating to find more valuables, but such actions could cause the mines to collapse.

events.name: Giant Statue

options.text: I shall have the statue repaired in my own image.
We should put the stone to better use.

events.text: These ruins are overshadowed by an enormous statue of a figure in a bold stance, legs astride what remains of the city gates and fist raised towards the sky. While it is still sturdy, time has eroded the features beyond any recognition.

events.name: Gold, like Mud

options.text: Give [character] what he needs.
Ask [character] to teach you how to extract such metals closer to home.
Have your people gather what they can.

events.text: Exploring the lands around the ruins, your explorers have discovered an incredible wealth of gold scattered below a shallow layer of earth. It is a place where precious metals seem as common as mud. Ever the Delver, [character] suggests taking the time to uncover these resources, although others in the court would prefer the fast injection of riches a fast plunder could bring. Is it worth the investment to uncover this distant wealth?

events.name: Great Migration

options.text: Commission scouts and send them in every direction.
Study this unknown tribe and widen our understanding.

events.text: Broken vessels and strange markings indicate that these ruins were once occupied by a tribe from beyond the sea. Such a discovery inspires you to expand beyond your realm, to new worlds...

events.name: Homeless Children

options.text: [rival] cannot become a home for charity.
We will shelter them.
We can always use citizens in [city].

events.text: Our explorers discover a group of orphaned, homeless, and hungry children hiding in the ruins. If we leave them, they will surely starve to death, but our cities are on the verge of overcrowding. There is room in our caravan for either salvaged stone or passengers. What would you have us do?

events.name: Hungry Lorekeepers

options.text: We will feed them and learn their skills.
We cannot afford to waste food on strangers.

events.text: Our explorers find a family of starving lorekeepers encamped in the ruins, surviving on scraps. Pleading for help, they offer to share their mastery of oratory in exchange for food. Will you agree to their offer?

events.name: Made to Measure

options.text: I will expect higher standards from now on.
Copy them, the best we can.

requirements.label: Greedy / Corrupt
tip: The leader must have one of: Greedy; Corrupt

options.text: This gives me an idea...

events.text: The ruined city lies empty, the shadow of a people long past. Yet their achievements live on. Within the rubble are rock-carved weights for trading, perfectly cut to ratio. Such accuracy is incredible, showing a repeated and consistent precision that even the craftsmen of your court are unable to match.

events.name: Monuments of Law

options.text: Send sages to learn what they can.
Send laborers to smash them into much needed rubble.

events.text: Our explorers come across a series of weathered monuments lost in the undergrowth. Upon closer inspection, the structures appear to be inscribed with the laws of a forgotten city. What should we do?

events.name: Necropolis

options.text: Allow the survivors to join us.
A terrible event, but I can learn from it.

events.text: Something awful happened here. Our scouts report that a once mighty city lies in ruins. The walls have been breached in multiple places and the population has been slaughtered. A few survivors remain, but far too few to even begin burying their dead.

events.name: Painted Walls and Stone-Carved Halls

options.text: So, this is the Buddha we have heard about.
How enchanting! Have artists recreate the paintings around the palace.
There is something in these that makes me want to strive to be better.

events.text: The caves have a peaceful quiet, held in the moment of stillness before breathing out. However, it is clear that the [unit] were not the first to find these hallowed halls. Each wall is covered in intricate paintings, depicting unknown figures caught in either pain or pleasure. Repeated throughout the paintings is a curious symbol of a flower where it seems a person ought to be. What could this symbolism mean?

events.name: Prophecy

options.text: It is a sign that I have been chosen.
Perhaps it is a distant ancestor.
It is a coincidence, nothing more.
I knew this would be here, I have divine powers!

events.text: Something in the newly discovered ruins has spooked our scouts, and they request that you visit the site at once. The court accompanies you to the weathered temple, where a series of ancient etchings seems to depict... you, [character]. Court scholars attempt to downplay the similarities as coincidence, but the resemblance is uncanny.

events.name: Religious Carvings

options.text: It must have come from a precursor of [religion] in the region.
Hand the site over to [religion] leaders and see what they make of it.
Move the art to [city] and establish [religion] shrine there.
"Carved art" sounds like "free stone" to me.

events.text: Walking among the ruins, your explorers are struck by the carved remnants of what looks like distinctly [religion] religious art. The site has clearly been abandoned for a long time, since before [religion] was known. Is this a mere coincidence, or something much more than that?

events.name: Research at Rest

options.text: Very intriguing indeed.
Invite the explorer to court so that we might further examine these new ideas.
Surely there are construction materials we can salvage from the site.

events.text: Seeking refuge, your injured [unit] discovers a long abandoned dwelling. While inspecting the unfamiliar architecture, your explorer notes a sophisticated form of small-scale irrigation that appears to have been used to water surrounding crops. Once rested up, your [unit] continues their journey and sends word home of their findings.

events.name: Ritual Performance

options.text: Expand our cities, but beware of gluttony.
Hold such performances ourselves.
Learn from his cunning.

events.text: In the ruins, we observe a ritual performance centering on the old city's patron god. He tricks minor deities into letting him eat them, but in the end they cut open his belly and kill him. What should we take away from this?

events.name: Rival Expedition

options.text: Capture the young noble, and seize the trove.
Offer apologies and promises of friendship.
Beg forgiveness for your crude maps of mighty [rival], and ask for corrections.

events.text: Amid the ruins our explorers discover an ancient burial site, brimming with a trove of valuables. Before anything can be done, however, an imperious young man at the head of his own expedition intrudes. "These riches, along with all these lands, fall under the domain of [rival]. Desist, and your trespass shall be graciously overlooked." What do you do?

events.name: Ruined Ambitions

options.text: The [family] ask that you [ambition].
The [family] want you to [ambition].
The [family] family suggest that you [ambition].

events.text: Your explorers send back word from the ruins of a beautiful palace ravaged by time. Beneath the throne is a stone, inscribed in an ancient form of. The regal inscription tells of a lost kingdom and the attempts of the to fulfill ambitions. The families are enraptured by this work of art and hope that you will strive to complete the ambitions that this previous nation could not.

events.name: Sacred Tomb

options.text: Leave the tomb undisturbed.
There will be no [title] but me. Destroy it!
Let us study their preservation rituals.

events.text: Our expedition approaches an ancient monument - the structure appears to be the tomb of a great leader. An inscription reads: "Passerby, whoever you may be, I was once King of Kings. Grudge me not, therefore, this piece of Earth that covers my body."

events.name: Seashore Find

options.text: This is a significant scientific discovery.
Our vivid fabrics will impress the world.
Other nations will pay for such a resource.

events.text: While exploring a remote stretch of seashore, we discover a curious shell scattered among the shallows. This shell, when ground into powder, produces a pleasant purple dye that is perfect for fabrics.

events.name: Shields Under the Stars

options.text: Offer [character] the chance to fight for a warrior-queen.
Raise a shrine to the Amazons in [city].
Use the tales of the Amazons to inspire your armies.

events.text: Your [unit] slowly approach the ruins under the cover of darkness, made wary by the fires flickering from within. As they get closer the glint of whirling metal catches in the firelight and shrill shouts fill the air, but these are no battlecries. Within the ruins the crouched troops see a group of women locked in a circular dance beneath the stars, each bearing a spear and shield which they spin and wield with ease. The tempo rises as the weapons swirl, until finally the music stops. As your people turn to leave they are interrupted by the women's leader, [character], "I thank you for not interrupting the rites. This is the tomb of one of the Amazons of old, sacred to Artemis."

events.name: Skirmish in the Ruins

options.text: Charge in to help the [rival] warriors.
Rush to the aid of the [tribe].
This is not our fight.
They must have found something valuable to fight over. Kill them all!

events.text: Your [unit] are climbing a low ridge to get the lay of the land when their attention is caught by the distant but unmistakable sound of sword on shield. Cautiously edging forwards, they see the ruins laid out below. At first there is no movement, then a single [rival] breaks from cover, closely followed by a [tribe] archer, who looses an arrow that misses by a hair’s breadth. Such scattered fighting appears to be going on throughout the ruins, although there are barely a half-dozen fighters on each side of the skirmish. As they spot your forces, each side cries out for help. Will your troops intervene?

events.name: Skittish Bandits

options.text: Agree to take him in and add him to your Court.
We don't need another merchant on the Court, but fund his trade mission so that we might profit from it.
Kill the merchant and take his supplies.

events.text: While exploring an ancient ruin, your forces come across a group of bandits harassing a man dressed in fine clothing, gallantly but vainly attempting to fight them off. Your group's sudden appearance, shouts and war cries startle the bandits and scatter them. The man bows low, grateful for the timely rescue. He thanks you profusely, explaining that he is a small, independent merchant. "Had you not arrived when you did, I fear they would have ended me." He says, offering himself and his services to your cause if you will but take him in.

events.name: Star Charts

options.text: Our scouts could use the direction.
Our astronomers are in need of inspiration.

events.text: Our explorers discover a cache of yellowed star charts in the ruins. The former inhabitants must have been a tribe of great navigators. Who should receive these charts?

events.name: Strange Scroll

options.text: Study the scroll to learn its secrets.
Find someone to decipher the text.
Something isn’t right, destroy it!

events.text: Sealed within a musty tomb, surrounded by strange signs and sigils, our scouts discover an ancient but surprisingly well-preserved scroll. Thinking this unsettling, they bring it to you for judgement. While the writing is in an unknown language, it is oddly simple. It feels as if you could quickly learn it if you devoted some time to the task.

events.name: Survivors

options.text: Recruit them as hardened explorers.

events.text: This village has only recently been sacked, and we discovered a band of survivors huddled in its ruins. These destitute refugees seem eager to abandon the wreckage of their old lives and join our nation, but they are strangers to our culture. What will you do with them?

events.name: The Jungle Depths

options.text: The trees can give us a tactical advantage.
Train specialists skilled in cutting through vegetation.
Stop complaining and force your way through!

events.text: As they cut through the dense overgrowth around the ruins, your [unit] leave a hand free to wipe the sweat from their faces as they battle the deep, wet, heat. Just as they reach the shelter of the ruins, the skies open. They are trapped there for days before realizing that the rain is not going to stop, continuing their long and slow trudge through the vegetation. Such reports are not uncommon. How are we to overcome the rains and vegetation of this land?

events.name: The King's Roads

options.text: Break down the roads for stone.
Study the technology.

events.text: Our expedition comes upon an impressive paved road system leading between wood structures that have long since rotted away. The engineering required to build such a site was far ahead of its time. What would you have us do with it?

events.name: The Riddle of the Gate

options.text: What's the riddle?
We have no time for riddles. Tear down the gate to enter the city.

events.text: We come across a guarded entrance to an ancient, ruined city. A majestic sphinx is sitting on an inscription that will help us open the gate.

events.name: The Seal of a Bull

options.text: I will adopt such a seal for myself.
Encourage the city artists to adapt this practice.
What strange creatures. I find myself rather inspired!

events.text: Exploring the ruins, your [unit] find a vast wealth of copper plates and stone stamps for impressing seals into clay. Are these the markings of a king or of proud artisans? A regular, yet unknown script lines each one, accompanied by an assortment of animals: Bulls, elephants, and a curious horse with a single horn.

events.name: Three Days of Solace

options.text: Swell!
Take this opportunity to devote one more day to military drills.

events.text: Battleworn and weary from the constant march, your troops take shelter at an abandoned encampment. During a three day rest they are able to treat the wounded, review recent battle outcomes, and even perform some light training exercises. When the time comes to march forth, your [unit] are filled with vigor and poise for the challenges ahead.

events.name: Tip to Tail

options.text: There can be no forest without tigers, and no tigers without a forest.
Return and do what you must. I will have these hides.
All life should be allowed to live in safety. Mark this land to be protected from hunting.

events.text: Cutting through the <p.is_sub.S1=SUBJECT_TILE_JUNGLE>Jungle<else>Trees<end> around the ruins, your [unit] are startled by a flash of orange and black. They soon realize that they are being followed by a giant cat, bound with muscle yet moving through the vegetation without a sound. It is not alone. The [unit] later report that upon reaching the ruins, there were a number of the creatures slinking over the stones and through the trees. Aware of being watched, the [unit] backed away, tremulous with awe but thankfully, for now, unharmed.

events.name: Unfamiliar Art

options.text: It should inspire us -- display it in [city]!
Perhaps someone else will appreciate it more.

events.text: Our scouts report discovering a strange sculpture amidst these ruins. While it is unlike any art produced in [rival], it holds a strange beauty. What should be done with it?

events.name: Veteran Soldier

options.text: Learn her military techniques.
Invite her to our court.

events.text: A scarred veteran soldier crouches in the ruins. She says that she once commanded the armies of a great nation, before a resistance brought it crashing down. She is willing to share her vast battlefield knowledge, if we are willing to listen.

events.name: Vulgar Speech

options.text: Display the graffiti in our palace yard.
Study the writing and try to replicate it.
"Vulgar" language should be lost. Replace it with my royal sigil.

events.text: Graffiti are scrawled across this ruined structure. One of our court scholars recognizes it as "vulgar speech," a Latin dialect used by the lower classes of several extinct tribes. There are very few examples of this traditionally unwritten language.

events.name: Cave In!

options.text: We will learn from our mistakes.

events.text: Our laborers' attempts to reopen the collapsed emerald mines have failed. Hillside supports crumbled, burying many men beneath the ruins and the rubble. Such a failed gambit has left the population shaken.

events.name: Emerald Mine Rebuilt

options.text: May this further cement my legacy.

events.text: After months of arduous labor, your crews of engineers have rebuilt the emerald mines discovered last year. Now that a base camp has been established in the distant hillside, our workers may brave the depths to bring new riches to the nation. Our gamble has paid off.

events.name: Mad Priestess

options.text: Sacrifice whatever is necessary to appease the fears of the people and to please the gods!
I reject her words. She was a mad woman, and I never was a fan of theatrics.

events.text: Driven to madness from her captivity and mourning the abandonment of her people, the High Priestess climbs atop a pyre and burns herself, shouting curses on your person and on our nation.

events.name: Strange Scroll: Revelation

options.text: It all makes sense now!

events.text: The scroll has taught you the Truth! You see the word in a new light, and your mind seems able to process everything in a new way, a better way! Abstract shapes whirl through your head, numbers and formulae flash before your eyes, and a crystalline clarity of purpose drives your thoughts!

events.name: Strange Scroll: Revelation

options.text: It all makes sense now!

events.text: You have come to understand the strange scroll. While at first it seemed to describe a different world, you have come to realise it is actually a series of allegories which reveal the unity of opposites. The world is at once one and many, and that it is just the opposite tension of the opposites that constitutes the unity of the One. “”.

events.name: Strange Scroll: Translation

options.text: Continue your studies.
Enough!

events.text: Your studies of the strange scroll have borne fruit. While at first the language it is written in made no sense, you have rapidly come to understand it. It almost feels as if the scroll wants to be read and is somehow helping you, but of course, that’s not possible. The scroll tells of. The things described are unlike anything you have ever heard of. Although you are learning a lot, studying the scroll is giving you a terrible headache.

events.name: The Riddle of the Sphinx

options.text: A man who crawls on four as a baby, walks on two as an adult, and uses a stick in old age.
This is the same riddle that Oedipus solved, but isn't he still most famous for marrying his mother?

events.text: The sphinx asks, "Which creature has one voice and yet becomes four-footed and then two-footed and finally three-footed?"

events.name: The Riddle of the Sphinx

options.text: Day gives birth to night just as night gives birth to day.

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

options.text: Only the gods know when the sun will rise and fall.

events.text: The sphinx ask, "My mother I bring forth, she brings forth me; I'm sometimes greater, sometimes less than she."

events.name: The Riddle of the Sphinx

options.text: My own face in the mirror cannot speak.
Mirrors are but a folly for the vain.

events.text: The sphinx asks: I look at you whenever you look at me; You see but I see not; no sight have I; I speak but have no voice; your voice is heard; My lips can only open uselessly.

events.name: The Riddle of the Sphinx

options.text: Only smoke gives me tears when I am not sad.
I wouldn't know anything about tears.

events.text: The sphinx asks: I am a black child sprung from a bright sire, A wingless bird, fleeting to heaven from earth. Each eye that meets me weeps, but not from grief, And in thin air I vanish at my birth.

events.name: Wrath of the Watchers

options.text: Do not acknowledge any such curse.
Make an offering to the gods, as penance.
This throne is plagued by spirits.

events.text: The ground shakes beneath [city]! Structures across the city suffer damage, but the number of dead is surprisingly low. In a strange coincidence, most of the victims were members of a famous expedition. They discovered the mysterious ruins known only as The Watchers. At our command, they destroyed the monoliths and recovered the useful stone. Perhaps that was a mistake...

label: Ruins

blurb: The scripted “send a character off to explore distant lands” chains. Some entries are follow-ups that only fire after an earlier expedition via an event link.

events.name: Hybris

options.text: We will take the risk, bring [character] to court.
Have the scholar serve as a for.
Leave [character] to his ramblings, but take the oracles.

events.text: [character] search has led to the edges of [rival], where he heard rumors of a scholar with a vast collection of oracular readings and prophesies from [religion]. [character] keeps the readings to himself, claiming that he is the only one capable of translating such divine utterances. This surely indicates a learned scholar, however [character] reports some... peculiarities when conversing with [character] that indicate the scholar may have had too much time in isolation with his prophesies.

events.name: Mani in the East

options.text: Bid him to continue exploring.
Have the prophet return home.

events.text: [character] has sent word that he has once more reached the distant land of Saka, where he has been met with a host of different religions and ways of thinking. Inspired to write by his discoveries, he has composed a new work in which he has dedicated to you. With his original goal complete, should [character] return to your court or continue exploring?

events.name: The First Disciple

options.text: Have him return, to hear the words of this disciple.
Refuse a new religion to take root and ask [character] to continue on his travels.

events.text: [character] has happened upon a lone traveler, who claims to be the first disciple of a great teacher and prophet. Upon hearing the tales, [character] is unconvinced about the ideas of this religion, but his devout nature draws him to want to document the faith and bring it back to [city].

events.name: Forest Druids

options.text: These rumors are highly disturbing. Demand that [character] return home immediately!

tip: As leader: +5% State Religion Spread Chance

options.text: I respect all pantheons. Let [character] stay and learn what he can from these druids.
Send priests out to study these Druids and see what we might learn from their ways.

events.text: Rumors abound in [city] that while exploring far-off sacred forests, [character] has abandoned the religion of his forefathers and converted to druidic paganism. One messenger has reported that druidic priests pack innocents into a towering wicker man and then set the effigy alight as part of their rituals! Such heresies are typical for barbarians, but that [character] should participate in them is simply beyond imagining. The [rival] people are concerned that [character] has been gone for too long and will soon permanently grow beyond the influence of his native land. Should [character] be permitted to continue living among the Druids of the forest?

events.name: Land of The Midnight Sun

options.text: Bring [character] home immediately!
Allow [character] to continue exploring.
Send an envoy to contact these giants!

events.text: Tales from [character]'s fantastic journeys have reached the capital, thrilling the people of [city] with stories of farthermost Thule, land of the midnight sun. These reports say that far to the north, beyond even the barbarous Celtic and Germanic Tribe, is a land of perpetual snow where the sun shines at midnight in the summer, and the winter is an unending darkness broken only by Aurora's chariot racing across the sky. They say that great giants roam there, and live for a thousand years. Could [character] have reached the legendary realm of Hyperborea?

events.name: Monsters of the Deep

options.text: Bring [character] back from these perilous adventures at once!
Stay out there [character]! You didn't think exploring would be easy, did you?
Let our scholars analyze these reports, and send sailors out to hunt and study these monsters.

events.text: The people of [city] listen in horror to the tales of [character]'s adventures on the open seas. They say an endless briny ocean, inhabited by gruesome beasts of the deep, marks the westernmost boundary of the known world. [character] reports that in the depths of the ocean lurk horrors beyond imagining. He tells tales of immense tentacled beasts that can crush a ship with a dozen sinewy arms and ravenous behemoths that consist of naught but a gaping maw of a thousand razor sharp teeth, with which they swallow men whole. [character] has grown wary of these dangers and desires to return home to the safety of [city], well beyond the reach of such nightmarish creatures of the sea.

events.name: The Ant's Gold

options.text: Send for [character] to return home. These tall tales of gold are a fool's pursuit.
Stay out there [character], and find a way to bring that gold home!
Let our scholars analyze these reports, and find in them some knowledge of the world.

events.text: All of [city] is enraptured with tales of [character]'s exploits in the land of the ant's gold! These reports say that far to the east, beyond even the tallest mountains, is a land of scorching deserts and unending sun where the sandy wastes are interrupted only by mounds of golden earth. Rumor is that giant ants live in that desert. They dig up the ground to build their homes and in doing so bring gold to the surface. The men then come when the sun is hottest and the ants are underground to haul the gold away with teams of yoked camels, fleeing with great haste lest they be caught by the jealous ants. Should [character] continue his travels in lands of such danger and opportunity?

events.name: A Dream in the Forest

options.text: Follow the feeling home.
Put the seed, and the dream, aside.

events.text: The smell of wet earth is overwhelming. The rushing patter of rain on the forest canopy invites a gentle reverie, even as [character] feels himself sink deeper in the loam. Breath ceases, and yet that brings not panic, but a strange sense of home and relief. [character] awakens with a start, hand grasping tight a small seed dug from the earth next to his bedroll. As the dream fades, the longing for that sense of home does not.

events.name: Converted on the Road

options.text: Recall [character] and stop any thought of [religion].
Invite [character] back to spread these intriguing ideas.
Allow [character] to continue on his way.

events.text: One finds all sorts of companions upon the road. [character] has been traveling with a holy man who calls himself a and speaks of the incomprehensible majesty of. [character] messages seem to speak more and more frequently of this [religion]. [character], a stalwart [religion], is aghast that a member of the royal family might be falling under the influence of a foreign, and undoubtedly immoral, religion. He begs you to bring [character] home, before it is too late.

events.name: Creatures of the Coast

options.text: Save the settlers and laborers.
Bring us the valuable metals.
Bring it all back, whatever the cost.

events.text: A weathered message arrives from distant lands. It is from [character], who has been traveling far beyond our borders. He is in need of urgent aid. [character]'s expedition has reached wild, undiscovered lands to the west, but it is now stranded. Ferocious undersea beasts block passage home. He wishes to know which ships should be highest priority: those carrying native laborers or those bringing rich western metals.

events.name: Exploration Ends?

options.text: [character] should continue to explore.

events.text: [character] has unexpectedly returned to the capital for a short visit. He seems weary from his travels, but is willing to continue exploring if the court desires it. What shall we command?

events.name: Exploration Ends?

options.text: [character] should continue to explore.

events.text: [character] has unexpectedly returned to the capital for a short visit. He seems weary from his travels, but is willing to continue exploring if the court desires it. What shall we command?

events.name: Eyes of Green

options.text: Send your finest workers to bring [character] and the statue back to [rival]
Encourage [character] to stay and study the statue for longer.

tip: As leader: -40 Opinion with all Religions

options.text: Bid him to break up the remains of the statue for resources.

events.text: Even gods must die. Cutting through the hills of a far off land, [character] comes across the broken statue of a deity lost to the winds of time. [character] feels a strong pull to this ancient god, writing at length of the pensive face with bright eyes of polished green stone.

events.name: From the Dead

options.text: Well, he has no further use for it.
May it lie here a thousand years more.

events.text: [character] finds himself in what must have been the tomb of an ancient king, perhaps an ancestor of the [tribe]? The king's armor stands seemingly untouched by time, a tempting prize for the difficult descent to this forgotten place.

events.name: Praying for a Safe Return

options.text: “May bring [character] home safely.”
Put your faith in [character] and his ability to make his own way home.

events.text: In the temple of [city] the work tirelessly to understand and communicate with the divine. [character] suggests visiting them, to offer a to for the safe return of [character], who is still.

events.name: The Land of Hairy Men

options.text: Order [character] home immediately.
Allow [character] to continue exploring.
Send men to study these fascinating creatures.

events.text: Tales from [character]'s fantastic journeys have reached the capital, thrilling the people of [city] with stories of tattooed warriors and black-teethed imps. The most terrifying tale comes from a small island, where a tribe of "hairy and savage" men threatened to overturn [character]'s boats. Truly, these tales are too incredible to be believed.

events.name: Towering Stones

options.text: Pry forth a stone, as a keepsake.
Leave the crumbling structures undisturbed.

events.text: The view of the ruins takes [character] breath away. Windswept and decaying ramparts stretch skyward, in all directions, and no doubt deep below as well. These ancient walls must have once towered higher than anything back in [rival].

events.name: Training with the Enemy

options.text: This is too dangerous. [character] should return at once.
May he fare well in the battles ahead.
Pay the mercenaries extra to keep [character] away from the worst of the fighting.

events.text: [character], long admiring the [rival] military practices, has joined the ranks of [rival] mercenary band while exploring. He reports that they are being contracted to fight in a large upcoming battle: Dangerous, but a good chance to learn more of their ways of fighting.

events.name: Under Attack

options.text: Help the soldiers make plans, and offer knowledge of the nearby terrain.
Rally a counterattack to free the rest of the [rival].

events.text: Much to [character] surprise, he stumbles upon a camp of [rival] far indeed from home. Around the fire he hears their tale of woe, captured on patrol by [tribe] warriors, only to escape during a river crossing while leaving their comrades and company banner behind.

events.name: [character] Travels

options.text: Enter [city].
Travel further, keeping to wilderness routes.
Turn back, toward the safety of [rival].

events.text: Wanderings far and wide have brought [character] to [rival] territory, not far from the city of [city]. A chance to resupply would be welcome, but the city carries its own dangers.

events.name: First Voyage

options.text: Instruct [character] to stay as an ambassador to [rival].
Use this opportunity to open new routes of trade.
So, we have even more enemies out there.

events.text: [character] sends word: After an arduous journey by sea and by land, he has reached the far-off lands of [rival] and is staying as a guest of [character] in the royal palace.

events.name: Silence

options.text: May he return soon.

events.text: It was a beautiful and happy day, full of hope, as the court stood on the shore to watch [character] sail over the horizon into the unknown. However, as time passes without word it becomes increasingly clear that not all is well. Only the gods know if he will be seen again.

events.name: Druidic Divinations

options.text: When ready, return to us with what you have learned.
Foreign creeds hold no interest for me. Go and find something of real value!

events.text: [character] has been living among the Druids for some time and has adopted their dress and customs. Fortunately, the disturbing rumors of human sacrifice are largely fabricated and [character] has not participated in, or even seen, such rituals himself. He has instead been occupied with the study of the many herbal and philosophical arts of the Druids, including the brewing of healing salves, and the Druidic belief in the immortality of the soul. [character] has become quite attached to his Druidic hosts and would like to stay among them for some time before returning home. Shall [character] be permitted to stay among the Druids?

events.name: Fishermen of the Western Sea

options.text: Come home, and bring that Fisher with you.
Keep exploring until you find something of real value!
Just come home without any locals in tow.

events.text: [character] sailed the westernmost ocean for some time, but to no avail. The sea was simply endless, and his ships dared not venture any further west. [character]'s party returned to the shore and stopped in a small fishing village of an unknown nation. He has befriended some of the locals there and asks to return to [city] with a Fisher in tow, or he can continue his travels.

events.name: Prince of Hindustan

options.text: Yes, [character], stay in India awhile. When you feel ready, return to us with what you have learned.
Foreign creeds hold no interest for me. Keep exploring until you find something of real value!

events.text: [character] scoured the desert wastes for the legendary ant's gold but found nothing other than sand, misery, and normal sized ants. There were camels though. So, he abandoned the avaricious quest for gold and continued on into the far eastern realm of Hindush, where he discovered riches of a different sort. [character] has now taken up residence in the court of a noble Indian prince and reports that the broad rivers and dense jungles of that land house a proud and learned people. He would like to stay in India a little while longer, absorbing the knowledge and spiritual beliefs of such an exotic realm, and its enigmatic pujaris, before returning home to regale all [city] with his learning. Will you permit [character] to stay at an Indian court before returning home, or shall he continue exploring?

events.name: Trappers from the Arctic Wastes

options.text: Come home.
Go on exploring elsewhere.

events.text: [character]'s travels in the Arctic have been fraught with danger. The nights are so cold that even under thick furs he feels the frost creep into his bones. A number of his companions have already succumbed to the weather. Their party spotted some shy native tribes that tend to flee from their presence, but none of them are giants. [character] has managed to trade some gold and trinkets with the locals for furs, the quality and size of which is allegedly most impressive. Should [character] return now, or continue exploring elsewhere?

label: Expeditions
